hypothesis.title: The Recoverable Window
hypothesis.question: Does musical continuity improve when analysis or transformation happens at the smallest window where the governing relation is recoverable?
hypothesis.hypothesis: If a musical structure is analyzed or transformed at the smallest window where its governing relation is recoverable, then the resulting material will preserve stronger continuity than material processed at a window that is too local, too global, or aligned to the wrong feature.
hypothesis.rationaleMd: Ice XXI shows that apparent local disorder can reveal periodicity at the right macroscopic scale [S1]. Stuttering precursor work shows that severe events can be forecast from a three-second prosodic window while other event types remain at chance [S2]. Omni2Sound shows that staged multimodal alignment can reduce video/text/audio task conflict [S3]. Infant-cry classification shows that short nonstationary biological signals may require fused F0, MFCC, STFT, and temporal-memory features [S4]. Tonnetz theory shows that harmonic relations become readable as graph incidence structures [S5]. STFT watermarking shows that selected phase and adjacent-bin log-magnitude degrees of freedom can carry recoverable information while remaining perceptually subtle [S6].

recipe.title: Recoverable-Window Composition
recipe.bodyMd: Build a 90-second study from one harmonic cell, one noisy or speech-like timbre, one rhythmic density curve, and one stereo or phase-sensitive texture. Compose versions that preserve order at different windows: local apparent disorder with larger periodicity, a prepared event with a three-second precursor versus an inserted event, picture/text/staged multimodal alignment, fused F0-MFCC-STFT feature preservation, Tonnetz-like graph path preservation, and a subtle hidden carrier in phase or adjacent spectral-band motion [S1, S2, S3, S4, S5, S6]. The test asks whether continuity follows the analysis window where the governing relation is actually recoverable.

parameters.value: STFT phase bins and adjacent-bin log-magnitude differences

dawChecklist: Create one 90-second source study with a harmonic cell, noisy or speech-like timbre, rhythmic density curve, and stereo/phase-sensitive texture.
Write a section that appears locally irregular but reveals periodicity across an eight- or sixteen-bar window.
Create one event with a three-second acoustic precursor and one matched inserted event without preparation.
Score the same cue picture-first, text/gesture-first, and with staged alignment, then compare modality bias.
Track F0 contour, spectral envelope, and short-time energy for the noisy timbre; render one variation preserving all three and one preserving only one.
Map the harmonic cell onto a small Tonnetz-like graph; render one version preserving path and another preserving chord labels only.
Embed a subtle continuity carrier in phase/stereo relation or adjacent spectral-band motion, then render a disturbed-carrier control.
Loudness-match and randomize all renders before judging continuity.

protocol.listeningContext: Studio monitors or neutral headphones, loudness-matched renders
protocol.listeningMethod: Blind randomized comparison with notes on which analysis window reveals the governing relation

notes: Disconfirming evidence: listeners only recover the claimed structure after reading the analysis, or transformations at the proposed recoverable window do not preserve audible continuity better than mismatched local/global controls.
